name: cat-categorization-map
title: Categorization Map & Generalization Edge
question:
How does the agent's final distance to the object vary with the object's
horizontal offset, for circles vs diamonds — and does the categorization hold
beyond the trained offset range?
hypothesis:
Across offsets the circle curve stays near zero (caught) and the diamond curve
stays high (avoided), giving two well-separated bands — Beer's categorization
plot — though generalization may fail past the trained range.
objective:
Sweep object offset from −8 to +8 for both shapes, measure final distance, and
render the categorization map.
claim:
Circles and diamonds form two separated bands across −8..+6 (catch vs avoid);
the separation collapses at offset ≥7 (untrained), an honest generalization edge.
description:
The committed seed is replayed over 33 offsets in [−8, 8] for each shape. The
map is the signature categorization plot of Beer (2003).

expected_behavior.name: category-separation-across-offsets
expected_behavior.condition: committed seed, offsets linspace(−8,8,33), both shapes
expected_behavior.rationale:
Over the trained band (−6..+6) circles end < catch radius and diamonds end
far (> 20); the two bands do not overlap. Outside training (|offset| ≥ 7)
diamonds are no longer reliably avoided — reported, not hidden.

findings.summary: Two separated bands across −8..+6; diamond avoidance fails at offset ≥7 (generalization edge).
findings.detail:
figures/categorization_map.png: the circle band hugs 0 (below the catch
radius) everywhere; the diamond band sits at 25–40 across −8..+6 then drops
to ~0.5 at offset ≥7, where the object sits at the edge of the sensor fan
beyond the training distribution.
